analysis: Chloroquine is primarily used for its anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects. It is well-established in the treatment of discoid lupus erythematosus, where it helps manage symptoms and prevent flare-ups. While chloroquine has some immunomodulatory properties that could theoretically benefit rheumatoid arthritis, it is not a standard or widely accepted treatment for this condition, with other medications being preferred. For infectious mononucleosis, chloroquine does not have a role, as this viral infection is typically self-limiting and managed with supportive care. Therefore, based on the consensus and available evidence, chloroquine is most clearly useful in treating discoid lupus erythematosus.
